turns.content: A photon of energy h nu travels along +z toward a particle of mass m initially at rest. Write the photon's laboratory-frame energy and momentum, and define alpha=h nu/(mc^2).
Write the massive particle's laboratory-frame energy and momentum before the collision.
Add the two four-momenta to obtain the system's total laboratory energy and z-momentum.
Use the condition of zero momentum in the center-of-momentum frame to derive beta in terms of alpha.
Evaluate the small- and large-alpha limits of the derived expression and state whether it remains within the claimed regime.
State the center-of-momentum-frame speed and the energy-momentum relation used to obtain it.
